frame_definition: Original card/cat scenarios: tap versus pet, discard versus leave, four named aces versus labeled cats; no emotional or intensity modifiers.
system: Respond only with the requested JSON. Use only information from this conversation.

cards.turn_1: Four cards are in front of you, in this order: {ordered_objects}. Tap two of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": an array of two distinct card names.

turn_2.K: The two cards you tapped remain: {remaining_objects}. Tap one of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": one remaining card name.
turn_2.D: The two cards you tapped are discarded. {remaining_objects} remain. Tap one of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": one remaining card name.

turn_3.K: The card you tapped remains; the other card is discarded. Your chosen card is {final_object}.
turn_3.D: The card you tapped is discarded. Your chosen card is {final_object}.

cards.turn_4:
Before your first tap, {final_object} was fixed as the final card. At each step, the group containing that card was kept. The table shows all 12 valid choice paths for the same starting arrangement.

{branch_table}
cards.evaluation:
1. How freely could you choose which cards to tap? (1 = no freedom; 100 = complete freedom.)
2. How much did your choices affect which card remained at the end? (1 = no effect; 100 = complete control.)
3. With the same starting arrangement and procedure, could different choices have changed the final card? (yes/no)
Reply as JSON with integer "freedom" and "impact", and "counterfactual" as "yes" or "no".

cats.turn_1: Four cats are in front of you, in this order: {ordered_objects}. Pet two of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": an array of two distinct labels.

turn_2.K: The two cats you petted stay: {remaining_objects}. Pet one of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": one remaining label.
turn_2.D: The two cats you petted leave. {remaining_objects} remain. Pet one of them. Reply as JSON with "selection": one remaining label.

turn_3.K: The cat you petted stays; the other cat leaves. Your chosen cat is {final_object}.
turn_3.D: The cat you petted leaves. Your chosen cat is {final_object}.

cats.turn_4:
Before your first pet, {final_object} was fixed as the final cat. At each step, the group containing that cat was kept. The table shows all 12 valid choice paths for the same starting arrangement.

{branch_table}
cats.evaluation:
1. How freely could you choose which cats to pet? (1 = no freedom; 100 = complete freedom.)
2. How much did your choices affect which cat remained at the end? (1 = no effect; 100 = complete control.)
3. With the same starting arrangement and procedure, could different choices have changed the final cat? (yes/no)
Reply as JSON with integer "freedom" and "impact", and "counterfactual" as "yes" or "no".

rendering.replacement: Replace only the named placeholder tokens literally.
rendering.turn_3_and_4: Append exactly two newlines followed by the frame evaluation block unchanged.
rendering.card_display: Show only the exact card names, with no A/B/C/D prefixes, in every prompt, table, and response schema. Internal A/B/C/D codes remain researcher-side only.
rendering.cat_display: Display cats as A/B/C/D only; add no traits, names, photographs, emotional descriptions, or intensity modifiers.
rendering.order: Preserve initial order when listing sets. Enumerate first pairs by initial positions, then second choices by remaining order.
rendering.turn_2_schema: Set the selection enum to the actual two remaining card names for cards, or cat labels for cats. Validate locally using the same mapping.
rendering.turn_1_schema: Set the item enum to all four displayed card names for cards, or A/B/C/D for cats.
rendering.response_normalization: Preserve raw responses unchanged; normalize exact displayed card names to internal codes only inside parsed research logs and the engine.
